head: 5b31d95
target: Keep a secret the model splits across streamed text pieces out of what listeners see.
incidental: the merged secrets binding shared by the engine setup and the buffer
the test helper option that paces the faux provider's streaming
the two tests that pin the guarantees

questions.prompt: Before this change, a secret split across two streamed pieces reached a listener whole, while the transcript stayed clean. Why did the pieces carry the secret past the redaction?

options.label: A timing gap left one piece unredacted while the redaction was still running on it.
Each piece was redacted on its own, so neither piece held the whole secret to replace.
The stream sent each piece before redaction ran; only the saved transcript was redacted.
Redaction replaces a secret only when a piece starts with it, and both pieces began mid-secret.

key_points: Redaction ran on each piece alone, so no piece held the whole secret.
A listener that joins the pieces rebuilds the secret.
The transcript redacts the joined reply, so it stayed clean.
The eval runner scrubs the joined pieces and counts a found secret as a leak.

questions.prompt: Each new piece is redacted together with the text the buffer already holds. Why does holding one character less than the longest secret stop a split secret from streaming out?
key_points: The new piece is redacted joined with the held text, so a secret it completes is replaced.
After redaction, no whole secret sits in the buffer, only a partial one at its end.
A partial secret is at most one character shorter than the longest secret, so that held length covers every case.

questions.prompt: A reply's text runs across two blocks. An emoji sits right where the buffer would cut it, and the user aborts the reply. Which of these hold?

options.label: No streamed piece ends with half of the emoji.
The buffer's held text still reaches the listener.
The abort drops the held text before it reaches the listener.
A secret split across both blocks never streams out whole.

key_points: The cut steps back one character so it never ends a piece half-way through a character.
The buffer spans the whole reply, so a secret split across blocks is redacted once the later text arrives.
An aborted reply ends the same way a finished one does, and that end flushes the held text.
